name: Utilities
one_liner: Regulated providers of electricity, gas and water whose returns are set by regulators on the capital they invest in networks.
how_it_makes_money: Regulated utilities earn an allowed return on equity on their rate base (invested capital), recovered through customer rates approved by state commissions. Fuel and purchased power are usually passed through to customers. Some players also run unregulated generation that sells into competitive wholesale markets.
revenue_formula: Regulated earnings = rate base × equity share × allowed return on equity
Revenue requirement = operating costs + depreciation + taxes + allowed return on rate base
cost_structure: Fuel and purchased power: large but largely passed through to customers
Operations and maintenance: crews, vegetation management, repairs
Depreciation on network and plant assets
Interest expense: utilities are heavily debt financed
margins: Returns are stable and bounded by regulation, with allowed ROEs typically around the high single to low double digits. Rate base growth, regulatory lag and constructive versus tough regulators drive differences.

key_metrics.name: Rate base
key_metrics.what: Invested capital on which the utility earns a regulated return; its growth drives earnings growth.

key_metrics.name: Earned vs allowed ROE
key_metrics.what: Gap reveals regulatory lag or cost overruns.

key_metrics.name: SAIDI / SAIFI
key_metrics.what: Outage duration and frequency, the core reliability measures.

key_metrics.name: Load growth
key_metrics.what: Growth in electricity demand, now rising after years of flat usage.

key_metrics.name: Capex plan
key_metrics.what: Multi-year investment that sets future rate base.

trends: Load growth returning, driven by data centers, electrification and reshoring
Massive grid capex for transmission, hardening and modernization
Wildfire and extreme weather liability reshaping risk and insurance
Affordability pressure as rates rise, tightening regulatory scrutiny
Coal retirements and renewables integration changing the generation mix
Renewed interest in nuclear, including life extensions and small modular reactors

case_angles.question: A utility wants to meet a surge of data center demand; how should it plan capacity?
How should a utility set rates for EV charging customers?
A utility's earned ROE is well below allowed; why and what to do?
Should a utility acquire a neighboring regulated utility?

interview_hooks: Who should pay for grid upgrades driven by data centers: the data centers or all ratepayers?
Does the regulated utility model encourage enough innovation?
Is nuclear a necessary part of a reliable decarbonized grid?
